key_insight: PatchTST is the strongest trained model for multi-horizon behavioral forecasting, but the zero-shot foundation model TimesFM is competitive or better, and participant-level fine-tuning substantially improves accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For mobile health systems, this suggests practical deployment can combine foundation models with lightweight personalization to improve forecasting from wearable and smartphone data.
method: Benchmarked six deep learning architectures plus two zero-shot foundation models and statistical baselines.
Evaluated step count, screen time, and sleep duration across 1–8 day forecasting horizons on three public datasets.
Tested participant-level fine-tuning and transferability across dataset sizes and temporal granularities.
evidence_signal: The study spans three public datasets with over 800 participants and reports per-feature performance across 1–8 day horizons.
watch_item: Results may depend on dataset characteristics and feature granularity, so zero-shot or personalized performance could shift when deployed on new populations or sensing pipelines.
paper_title: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Horizon Behavioural Forecasting for Mobile Health
